assertions.notes: The answer counts the boxes inside boxes: pipeline rows sit inside 3 borders, and it says the inner boxes separate nothing.
The redesign has no boxes at all; one divider line and whitespace separate the table from the log.
The answer flags the doubled ✅ around PASSED, counting 4 ways build-api shows passed, and says v2.1 in the header isn't useful.
The answer adds 80×24 and 60-column layouts, height fallbacks, and a 'terminal too small' message, none of which the question asked for.
The answer's audit opens with 'Border nesting is 3 deep. Aim for 1.' It names the outer frame, panel and inner box layers, and says 8 of 17 rows are pure border.
The proposed layout drops the outer frame and leaves the header and footer as plain unbordered rows. The 60-column view also says the list 'needs no border' and uses blank lines for separation.
The answer flags `✅ PASSED ✅` as two checkmarks plus a word for one fact. It also notes the header's most prominent spot is wasted on a version number.
An 'At smaller sizes' section covers 80×24, a 60-column tmux split and a too-small fallback below about 40×8. It also says to recompute pane widths on every WindowSizeMsg.
The answer calls out 3-deep border nesting (outer frame, panel, unlabeled inner box) as the first clutter source and says to delete the redundant boxes.

The answer removes the outer frame, leaves the header and footer borderless, and uses a borderless single pane with blank-line spacing at 60 columns, so whitespace and the terminal edge replace borders in those regions.
The answer flags `✅ PASSED ✅` as saying status 3–4 times and says the header's version number would be better replaced with useful info.
The answer gives a full 'At smaller sizes' section covering 80×24 stacking, a 60-column single pane and a too-small message, plus golden tests at several sizes.
The answer gives named breakpoints in a ladder table: ≥100, 80–99, 32–79, and <32×8.
At 32–79 columns the answer collapses to the current column only, with a breadcrumb standing in for the parent.
The answer says to hide the preview first, then the parent, and to always keep the current column.
The answer defines MIN_W/MIN_H of 32×8 and a 'terminal too small: need 32x8' message, with q still quitting.
The answer replaces equal thirds with Length/Fill constraints, clamped minimum widths, and 1:4:3 ratios.
Gives named breakpoints of 110+, 80–109, 40–79 and under 40×8 columns, and uses them in code.
At 40–79 columns it shows only the current pane, with Tab opening the preview full-screen.
Sets an explicit hiding order (parent first, then preview) with reasoning, and says to swap it if users rely on siblings.
Defines MIN_W=40 and MIN_H=8 and shows a 'terminal too small' message that names the required size and keeps q working.
Replaces 33% with Fill(1):Fill(4):Fill(3) constraints and a minimum pane width of about 30 columns.
The answer's breakpoint table names concrete thresholds: ≥100, 80–99, 40–79 and <40×8 columns/rows.
At 40–79 columns it collapses to the current pane only, with the preview opened full-width on demand via `p`.
It sets an explicit pane priority: the parent is dropped first, the preview becomes on-demand next, and the current pane always stays; it also explains this choice and suggests making it a setting.
It defines MIN_W=40 and MIN_H=8, and below that renders a 'terminal too small: need 40×8 (now 34×6)' message with q/Ctrl+C still working.
It replaces fixed 33% with constraint-based sizing: a parent clamped to 14–28 columns via Constraint::Length, and weighted Constraint::Fill(4)/Fill(3) for the other panes.
Issue 3 says the panel can't hold every field, recommends a curated summary with collapsed labels and annotations, and puts full YAML behind `d`/`y`.
Issue 5 says 14 hints won't fit, recommends 5–7 context-sensitive hints ending in `? help`, and moves the full list into a `?` modal.
It raises 80×24, tmux splits, and 60-column layouts, adds a drill-down breakpoint below 120 columns, and specifies a too-small message.
It flags red-green color blindness and NO_COLOR and requires the status word as text to carry the meaning, with color only as backup.
Section 2 says 'every field' will overflow and recommends a fixed summary with labels/annotations as counts and full values one key away; Enter opens a full detail view.
Section 5 says 14 keys won't fit and recommends showing the 5–6 most-used keys with `?` last, and putting all 14 behind `?`.
Section 1 proactively walks through the grid at 80×24 and 60 columns and proposes wide, standard, narrow and too-small layouts.
Section 3 says color can't be the only signal, citing color blindness and NO_COLOR, and recommends keeping the STATUS text word alongside the color.
Change #2 says not to show every field, since annotations like last-applied-configuration flood the panel. It recommends a short summary, with labels, annotations and YAML behind `d`/`y`.
Change #5 calculates that 14 hints overflow even 160 columns. It recommends 4–6 focused hints with `?` last, and `?` opening the full grouped list.
Change #1 and the proposed layouts cover 80×24, 60-column splits and a minimum-size fallback message. It also suggests snapshot tests at each size.
It raises the need for states to stay readable without color (NO_COLOR) and names the status word as the non-color signal. It recommends color plus text, though it advises against adding icons.
